newsitem.title: USA: Disney shareholders approve Eisner contract.
newsitem.headline: Disney shareholders approve Eisner contract.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. shareholders approved a new contract Tuesday for Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Eisner despite opposition from critics who called the compensation package excessive, the company said.
Shareholders also approved the re-election of five members of the board of directors and approved a change in the cash bonus compensation for top Disney executives, Disney said.

More than 87 percent of the shares were voted to approve the re-election of the five directors, including Roy Disney, nephew of Walt Disney. But, reflecting concerns about the board's independence, support for the re-election was withheld by 12.7 percent of shares.

Eisner, who took the unusual step of defending the board during lengthy introductory comments, responded to the company's critics, saying many board members helped keep Disney intact when it was the subject of takeover attempts in 1984.
"This is an active board," Eisner said. "One that is supportive but also demanding."
Eisner has been under fire for hiring former Hollywood talent agent Michael Ovitz as president in 1995, only to pay him a huge severance package a year later when Ovitz resigned.
In a rare admission, Eisner called the decision to hire Ovitz "a mistake in judgment" and he vowed not to let it happen again.

Eisner said the cost of buying out Ovitz' contract, "as high as it was," would have been much higher if we had stayed the unstayable course." Ovitz received nearly $39 million in cash and stock options on 3 million shares currently worth about $56 million.

During the meeting, which lasted more than four hours, Disney officials were questioned -- at times shouted at -- by shareholders who demanded to know why the company's board agreed to the settlement for Ovitz and why they agreed to a new 10-year contract for Eisner that critics claim is worth $400 million.
"I have nothing against Mr. Eisner," said one shareholder. "He's done a fine job, but I think (this contract) is a little too lucrative."
"He's paid more than the president of the United States," added another shareholder.
